annotations.title: Is this AI model id retired, and when does it shut off?

description: Ask this before you pin, recommend or migrate off a model id. Give the id exactly as it goes in the config — "gpt-4o", "anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0", "gemini-1.5-pro-002", "mistral-large-2407" — and get whether it is retired, the shutdown date the provider published, the replacement the provider names, and a verbatim quote of the page that says so. Where several hosts sell the same id you get every one of them, and earliest_announced_shutdown is the date a migration actually has to meet: on 34 records a second host switches the model off EARLIER than the record's primary source does. An id we hold nothing for returns found: false and no date, which means not in our records, never "still supported".

model_id.description: The model id as the provider writes it. Matched exactly, then case-insensitively, then against the alternative name a record's own id prints, then against the human-readable model name. Never as a substring: "gpt-4" does not answer for "gpt-4o".

provider.description: Optional. Narrow to one provider's schedule, matched case-insensitively as a substring of the provider name ("bedrock", "azure", "groq"). Leave it out to see every host's clock for this id, which is usually what you want.

name: model_status

answer.description: One sentence, computed here from the records below, for a caller that needs a line rather than a structure.

as_of.description: The UTC date every "has it passed" answer here was computed against.

earliest_announced_shutdown.description: The soonest shutdown date any source states for this id, with the page and quote that state it. THE FIGURE TO PLAN AGAINST. Floors and no-date sentences are excluded; null where no source gives a date. A negative days_away means at least one host has already switched the model off.

found_on_record.description: The record_id this date was found on, which is not the same as the provider that stated it.

source_host.description: The host of source_url, for a caller that wants to name who said it in one word. Taken from the URL, not inferred.

stated_by.description: The provider whose own page states this date. NULL where the date comes from a second source the record cites rather than from the record's own provider — read source_url for who said it. A second source's date is never attributed to the record's provider.

matched_on.description: Which rung of the ladder matched. Absent when nothing did.

also_reported.description: Values for this record reported by a SECOND source, each with its own source_url and source_quote. Cite these to the page they name, never to the record's primary source.

days_until_shutdown.description: COMPUTED HERE: whole days from as_of to shutdown_date_iso. Negative means the date has passed. Null where there is no date or the date is a floor.

deprecation_announced.description: When the provider announced it, as printed.

lifecycle_status.description: The provider's OWN word, verbatim — "Retired", "Removed", "Deprecated", "Legacy", "EOL", "GA", "Preview". Not normalised: read `status` for our comparable reading of it. One value is ours and not a provider's: "Retirement date passed", on a model the provider's page still lists as available after the retirement date it prints.

model_id.description: The API model id, exactly as the provider writes it.

model_name.description: The human-readable name, where the provider gives one.

platform_scope.description: Which platform or deployment the date applies to.

provider.description: Whose schedule this record is. The same model id can appear under several providers with different dates.

record_url.description: This record's own page on referencesource.org.

regions.description: Where the provider scopes this schedule, where it does.

replacement_model.description: The replacement the PROVIDER names, where it names one. Null where it does not — no replacement is ever suggested here.

shutdown_date.description: The shutdown or retirement date exactly as the provider prints it, in whichever of seven formats that is.

shutdown_date_is_a_floor.description: True where the provider said "not sooner than" or "or later". The model will not go BEFORE that date; it says nothing about when it will.

shutdown_date_iso.description: COMPUTED HERE from shutdown_date, not text from the provider. Null where the provider stated no date, or a sentence we would have to guess at.

shutdown_dates_stated.description: Every shutdown date stated for this model id, each cited to the page that states IT and not to the record's primary source. More than one entry means the hosts disagree, which is the normal case for a model sold by several of them.

as_printed.description: Exactly as the provider prints it.

date.description: ISO form, computed here from as_printed. Null where the provider stated no date.

is_a_floor.description: True where the provider stated a floor, not a date ("Not sooner than April 16, 2027"). Such a date is not a retirement date and is excluded from upcoming_retirements.

source_quote.description: Verbatim text from that page containing the value.

source_url.description: The page the value was read from.

status.description: COMPUTED HERE as of as_of, from the provider's word and the provider's date. shut_down: the provider's word is terminal, or the date it published has passed. scheduled: a real future date. no_date_announced: in our records, but with no date to compare. Read status_basis for which of the two it was read from.

status_basis.description: The one sentence saying what `status` was read from, naming the provider's word and date. Where those two disagree it says so.

similar_ids_in_our_records.description: Only on a miss. Ids in this register containing the string you asked about. NOT AN ANSWER about any of them — no date and no status is attached, because you did not ask about them. Call model_status again with one if it is the id you meant.

title: Is this AI model id retired, and when does it shut off?
